about: Design-production status for the low-fidelity wireframes, and nothing else. It says which surface is in which review batch, which artefacts exist, in which language and viewport, which states they cover and how far the review has gone. It restates no requirement: the surface, its rows and its states are in design/inventory/surfaces.json, and every entry here points at one by its canonical id. Checked by tools/design_wireframes.py. The format and the workflow are in README.md and workflow.md beside this file.

review_statuses.briefed: A brief is generated. Nothing is drawn.
review_statuses.exploration: Being explored in the calibration set or in its batch. More than one treatment may exist.
review_statuses.candidate_selected: The owner chose the treatment to carry forward. Not yet drawn in full.
review_statuses.wireframed: Drawn in full: every listed state, both languages where they apply, mobile and desktop.
review_statuses.reviewed: The owner reviewed it and the batch is closed. Still neutral, and not approved interface design.
review_statuses.not_applicable: Not wireframed: a provider's interface, or a surface that exists only at high fidelity.

cell_statuses.not_applicable: Does not apply to this surface.

directions.label: Clean Premium Commerce
directions.approach: Calm and restrained. Lower density, generous whitespace, a quiet header, large product imagery, and merchandising content used sparingly so the product carries each view.

directions.label: Editorial Modern Retail
directions.approach: Composed like a publication. Larger editorial blocks set among the products, strong typographic hierarchy, imagery that dominates, and grids that vary rather than repeat.

directions.label: Dynamic Contemporary Ecommerce
directions.approach: Energetic and efficient. Higher density, more products in view, prominent merchandising rails and badges, a utility-forward header, and the purchase actions kept close at hand.

directions_note: The labels are descriptive only. They are three structural approaches to hierarchy, density, composition and interaction, not three brand identities. All three satisfy the same scope, draw the same states, keep every pattern the contract fixes, and stay neutral. They may differ only in presentation and in interaction choices that are genuinely open. None adds a feature.

calibration.purpose: Establish the structural ecommerce direction on a representative set of first-release customer surfaces, in three directions, before it is carried across the inventory. Exploration: it locks nothing until the owner selects.

frames.name: Global desktop frame: header, navigation, search and footer
Mobile shopping composition: listing, filters, product and add to cart

selection.note: The owner chooses a, b or c, or one of them with named elements from another. Selecting a structural direction is not approval of the brand identity and not approval of the interface design.

batches.name: Product page, gallery and purchase actions
Additions to the standard administration, and reports

entries.not_in_low_fidelity: Premium visual treatment and discount presentation cannot be shown in a neutral wireframe. It is designed at high fidelity, once the brand identity is supplied.
